text: Josephine was kneeling before the closed door with her lips to the keyhole, begging Louise to open it before she made herself ill. <break time="0.8s" /> Go away, I am not making myself ill, answered Louise, who was drinking in the very elixir of life through that open window. <break time="0.8s" /> Her imagination was running wild, and she thought of all the spring days and summer days that would be her own. <break time="0.8s" /> She breathed a quick prayer that life might be long, and yet only yesterday had she shuddered at that very thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Her eyes shining with a feverish triumph, she at last rose and opened the door to her sisters pleading. <break time="0.8s" /> She carried herself unknowingly like a goddess of Victory, and the two sisters went down the stairs, with her arm around Josephines waist. <break time="0.8s" /> Richards was waiting for them below when someone opened the front door with a latchkey, and in stepped Brently Mallard himself, carrying his bag and umbrella. <break time="0.8s" /> He had been far from the accident, so he stood amazed at Josephines piercing cry and at Richards quick motion to hide him from his wife. <break time="0.8s" /> But Richards was too late, and when the doctors came, they said that she had died of heart disease, of the joy that kills.
